summary: For elastic/apm-server standalone verification, the reliable end-to-end path is: start-local Elasticsearch+Kibana, install the bundled APM package via Fleet, run the official standalone apm-server image with mounted config, verify authenticated /app/observability/services HTML plus a referenced asset, post the upstream minimal.ndjson fixture to /intake/v2/events for HTTP 202, then confirm Elasticsearch hits for the fixture service.
symptom: Need a current, reproducible official-path verification for standalone APM Server that proves both UI delivery and real intake/indexing behavior.
root_cause: Standalone APM Server depends on external package assets and current Kibana Observability routes rather than older APM-specific assumptions.
successful_path: Initialize Fleet in Kibana, install the bundled apm package version matching the stack, run docker.elastic.co/apm/apm-server with output.elasticsearch and apm-server.kibana configured to the local stack, verify / returns publish_ready true, POST source/testdata/intake-v2/minimal.ndjson for 202, and query Elasticsearch for service.name=1234_service-12a3 while also checking authenticated /app/observability/services and one CSS asset.
fix: Use /api/fleet/setup and /api/fleet/agents/setup before checking package state.
Install /api/fleet/epm/packages/apm/<stack-version> when status is not_installed.
Use the current Observability services route for UI verification instead of /app/apm.
precheck: Confirm Kibana reports the apm package status before launching standalone apm-server.
Verify the APM package version matches the Elasticsearch/Kibana stack version.
Use the upstream minimal.ndjson fixture for a deterministic intake test.
anti_pattern: Skipping Fleet package installation and assuming standalone apm-server alone will provision the needed assets.
Relying only on open ports without proving intake acceptance and indexed APM documents.

summary: Piwigo verification is strong when it goes beyond reachability and checks installer completion, authenticated admin access, a critical asset, initialized database content, and required PHP extensions.
symptom: The app is up and returns HTML, but deployment quality is still uncertain until initialization and admin functionality are proven.
root_cause: Piwigo can serve the installer or public shell before the gallery is proven usable, so status-only checks understate deployment risk.
successful_path: Verify `GET /` changes from an install redirect to the welcome/login shell, post the installer successfully, log in as the created admin to `admin.php`, fetch `themes/default/theme.css`, confirm MySQL version and admin row existence, and confirm `gd`, `mbstring`, `pdo_mysql`, and `zip` in-container.
fix: Use a session-backed POST to `identification.php` for authenticated admin verification.
Query `piwigo_users` for the created admin account after installation.
Check required PHP extensions from inside the running app container.
precheck: Force localhost HTTP checks through `curl --noproxy '*'` on this host before diagnosing app failures.
anti_pattern: Do not stop at `docker compose ps` or a root `HTTP 200` as proof of success.
Do not ship a bundle without proving authenticated admin access after redeploy.
quick_checks: `curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` should return `200` after install, not a redirect to `install.php`.

summary: For image-first ejabberd deployments, the reliable verification path is authenticated WebAdmin HTML plus a referenced asset, expected root 404, XMPP TCP reachability, and user/password/status checks run with ejabberdctl as the ejabberd user.
symptom: Simple reachability checks can miss real operator regressions or can report false bundle failures when inherited health checks or ejabberdctl commands run as root.
root_cause: The usable operator surface is the authenticated /admin/ WebAdmin path, and the container runtime expects admin CLI operations from the ejabberd user rather than root.
successful_path: Verify /admin/, /admin/server/<host>/, /admin/style.css, expected root 404, XMPP port reachability, and ejabberdctl registered_users, check_password, and status executed as ejabberd; for the portable bundle, override the inherited healthcheck to use ejabberdctl status as ejabberd.
fix: Use admin Basic Auth for WebAdmin and CSS asset verification.
Run bundle health checks and `ejabberdctl` verification inside the container as the `ejabberd` user.
Keep the expected root `404` as a positive sanity check because `/admin/` is the documented entrypoint.
Run bundle health checks and ejabberdctl verification inside the container as the ejabberd user.
Keep the expected root 404 as a positive sanity check because /admin/ is the documented entrypoint.
precheck: Confirm the seeded admin credentials before using WebAdmin verification.
Use `curl --noproxy '*'` on this host for localhost checks.
Do not classify `/` returning `404` as a failure when `/admin/` is healthy and documented.
Use curl --noproxy '*' on this host for localhost checks.
Do not classify / returning 404 as a failure when /admin/ is healthy and documented.
anti_pattern: Treating the unauthenticated `/admin/` Basic Auth challenge or the root `404` as deployment failure.
Running inherited bundle health checks as root and trusting the resulting `nodedown` signal without testing as the `ejabberd` user.
Treating the unauthenticated /admin/ Basic Auth challenge or the root 404 as deployment failure.
Running inherited bundle health checks as root and trusting the resulting nodedown signal without testing as the ejabberd user.
quick_checks: `docker exec <container> sh -lc "su -s /bin/sh ejabberd -c 'ejabberdctl registered_users example.org && ejabberdctl status'"`
docker exec <container> sh -lc "su -s /bin/sh ejabberd -c 'ejabberdctl registered_users example.org && ejabberdctl status'"

summary: osTicket verification is materially stronger when it crosses the public intake UI and the staff queue, not just the public landing page.
symptom: A 200 response on / can hide an uninitialized or partially broken helpdesk deployment.
root_cause: osTicket baseline usability depends on both client-side ticket intake and status pages and the authenticated staff queue.
successful_path: Verify /, /open.php, /view.php, /scp/login.php, and a critical asset, then authenticate as staff and confirm a known ticket appears in the queue. For bundle validation, also confirm the restored database still contains the admin user and expected ticket count.
fix: Check page bodies for expected osTicket strings, not status codes alone.
Require a successful staff login redirect and authenticated queue evidence.
Preserve one real ticket as cross-boundary proof from client flow to staff UI.
precheck: Use curl --noproxy '*' for localhost verification to avoid proxy contamination.
Capture a critical CSS asset check alongside HTML checks.
anti_pattern: Do not accept only HTTP 200 from / as proof of usability.
Do not stop after anonymous ticket creation without confirming staff-side visibility.
quick_checks: Confirm Welcome to the Support Center on / and Contact Information on /open.php.
Confirm staff login returns 302 to index.php and the queue contains the expected ticket subject and requester.

summary: For FreeScout, a usable deployment is best proven with a real admin login, a mailbox list check, and a mailbox creation or mailbox page check rather than root/login status codes alone.
symptom: HTTP checks alone can say the app is up while operator functionality is still unproven.
root_cause: FreeScout is an operator-facing web app where the meaningful baseline is authenticated mailbox management, not anonymous root reachability.
successful_path: Verify GET /login -> 200 HTML, fetch a critical CSS asset, log in with the installer-created admin, then confirm /mailboxes and /mailbox/<id> load and preserve the created Support mailbox.
fix: Use session-backed login verification instead of curl-only anonymous probes.
Pair HTTP status checks with content-level checks that reject Whoops, DriverException, Mix manifest not found, and Access denied bodies.
quick_checks: After login, GET /mailboxes should contain the created mailbox name.
GET /mailbox/<id> should return 200 HTML without framework exception signatures.
evidence: The primary deployment and the redeployed portable bundle both preserved admin login and the Support mailbox pages.

summary: For HedgeDoc 1.10.x, a strong primary and portable verification path is root HTML plus one build asset, POST /new with raw markdown and Content-Type text/markdown, note HTML, download parity, note info title, _health ready=true, and status counters.
symptom: A HedgeDoc deployment appears healthy but basic note-editing behavior has not been proven.
root_cause: Status and readiness checks alone do not validate the user-facing Markdown note flow.
successful_path: Verify the landing page HTML, fetch one referenced /build asset, create a note through POST /new using raw markdown, confirm the created note HTML, require /download content parity, check /info metadata, and confirm _health plus /status.
fix: Use Content-Type text/markdown with POST /new instead of form encoding.
Treat /download content parity as the proof that imported note content was persisted.
Keep localhost verification curls on this host on --noproxy '*'.
precheck: Search the official docs for the supported note creation request shape before scripting verification.
Fetch one referenced frontend asset from the root HTML before accepting the UI as complete.
anti_pattern: Accepting only GET / or /status as proof of a working HedgeDoc deployment.
Using form-encoded POST /new and assuming the redirected editor proves note persistence.

summary: For HedgeDoc 1.x / codimd-server stable deployments, the strongest primary and portable verification path is root HTML plus one referenced frontend asset, guest note creation via POST /new, /download parity, /info title check, and a local-account login that changes the root UI to New note and Sign Out.
symptom: A HedgeDoc deployment appears healthy, but baseline note editing and signed-in UI behavior have not been proven.
root_cause: Status-only or root-only checks miss broken note persistence, broken asset URLs, and broken local-account behavior.
successful_path: Verify the root HTML shell, fetch one referenced build asset, create a guest note with POST /new using text/markdown, require exact /download parity and /info title, then login with a registered local account and confirm the root UI exposes New note and Sign Out.
fix: Use POST /new with Content-Type text/markdown for note-flow verification.
Require exact download parity instead of only loading the note page.
Confirm the authenticated root UI changes state after local login.
precheck: Read the stable 1.x API docs for /new, /download, and /info before scripting verification.
Bypass host proxies with curl --noproxy '*' for localhost verification on this host.
anti_pattern: Accepting only GET / or /status as proof of a working HedgeDoc deployment.
Treating guest note creation alone as sufficient when local account auth is enabled.
quick_checks: curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ | rg 'New guest note|Sign In'

summary: For wkhtmltopdf-style CLI renderers, strong primary and portable verification should prove a real conversion by generating PDF and PNG artifacts from HTML and validating them with pdfinfo, pdftotext, and file rather than accepting version output or a non-empty blob.
symptom: A renderer can report the expected version yet still ship weak or misleading artifact evidence.
root_cause: Version output and file size alone do not prove that the rendered document is a valid PDF with the expected content or that the image output is structurally correct.
successful_path: Run a deterministic verify-conversion.sh against a known sample HTML, require both wkhtmltopdf and wkhtmltoimage outputs, confirm the PDF with pdfinfo Pages: 1 and pdftotext expected text, and confirm the PNG with file output and nonzero size.
fix: Export the generated artifacts to the deliverable and inspect them on the host with pdfinfo and pdftotext.
Keep PDF and PNG checks in both primary and portable verification paths.
precheck: Have a deterministic HTML sample committed in the deliverable.
Do not rely on in-container file output alone when it disagrees with stronger artifact inspection tools.
anti_pattern: Do not accept wkhtmltopdf --version as the only proof of a working deployment.
Do not ship the bundle without checking the post-redeploy artifacts against the same content-level assertions.
quick_checks: pdfinfo output.pdf should report Pages: 1 and Creator: wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6.1.
pdftotext output.pdf - should contain the expected sample text.
file output.png should report PNG image data.

summary: For apache/apisix, a strong verification gate combines the embedded Dashboard UI shell, one referenced UI asset, an Admin API route read/write check, and a proxied gateway request through that route.
symptom: Simple container-up or root-port checks can miss missing UI delivery or broken route proxying.
root_cause: APISIX exposes separate operator and gateway surfaces, so a single status check does not prove end-to-end usability.
successful_path: Verify /ui/ for HTML, fetch one referenced /ui/assets resource for HTTP 200, create or read a route object through /apisix/admin/routes/1 with X-API-KEY, and require a gateway request through that route to return the upstream body.
fix: Use curl --noproxy '*' for localhost verification on this host.
Treat the root gateway 404 before route creation as expected, not as a deployment failure.
Gate success on a real proxied response body after route creation.
precheck: Inspect proxy-related environment variables before trusting localhost curl failures.
Capture one asset path from the UI HTML and verify it directly.
anti_pattern: Do not accept only GET /ui/ or only GET /hello as the full verification gate.
Do not interpret gateway root 404 as broken when no matching route exists yet.
evidence: DP_LOGS/apisix/deploy.log records /ui/, asset, Admin API route, and /hello checks.
DP_LOGS/apisix-final/summary.md records the same checks after migration re-deploy.

summary: For osCommerce v4, strong primary and portable verification should prove the splash storefront, one real storefront route, one asset, and an authenticated admin login to /admin/index instead of accepting the installer page or a root-only HTTP 200.
symptom: The root URL can return HTML even when the deployment still points at the installer or when backend/admin behavior is not yet proven.
root_cause: osCommerce exposes both a splash storefront and a backend, so root reachability alone does not prove catalog routing, asset delivery, or operator usability.
successful_path: Verify GET / returns HTML, verify a referenced storefront asset returns 200, verify a friendly storefront route such as /furniture/ returns 200 with category content, verify admin login page 200, then perform a real admin login and require /admin/index to return 200 HTML.
fix: Include /furniture/ or another real storefront route in both primary and portable verification.
Keep a real admin session-backed login in the verification gate.
precheck: Disable or rename install/ before accepting the deployment as finished.
Bypass host proxies with curl --noproxy '*' during localhost verification on this host.
anti_pattern: Do not accept only GET / as proof of a usable osCommerce deployment.
Do not ship a final bundle without proving admin dashboard access after redeploy.
quick_checks: Admin login should 302 to /admin/index and the dashboard should return 200 with backend navigation content.

summary: Strong Hasura verification combines the console shell, the console's referenced asset loader URL, metadata export for the default source/tracked table, and a real GraphQL read/write check against initialized rows.
symptom: A bare health check or console 200 is insufficient to prove that Hasura is initialized and usable.
root_cause: Hasura can serve health and shell responses before you have verified the metadata source, tracked tables, and real GraphQL operations that represent operator success.
successful_path: Verify root redirect, console HTML, the resolved assetLoader.js.gz URL from assetsPath+assetsVersion, export_metadata showing source default and table public.notes, then run insert_notes_one and read back the notes rows.
fix: Resolve the actual asset loader URL from the console HTML instead of guessing a same-origin asset path.
Require metadata export and GraphQL row checks alongside the console/UI checks.
precheck: Use curl --noproxy '*' for localhost verification on this host.
Expect the built-in console to reference official CDN assets by default.
anti_pattern: Do not accept only /healthz or /console HTTP 200 as Hasura success.
Do not guess a console asset path like /assetLoader.js without parsing the HTML's assetsPath and assetsVersion.
quick_checks: curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ should show a redirect to console.
curl --noproxy '*' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/console should include serverVersion and assetsVersion.
POST /v1/graphql with notes(order_by:{id:asc}) should return the preserved rows.

summary: For Elasticsearch bundles, status checks are insufficient; require authenticated HTTPS root, green cluster health, smoke index write/search, and a read-only user query on the restored data.
symptom: A node can be running and reachable while credentials, system indices, or restored data are still not usable.
root_cause: Basic reachability and unauthenticated auth-challenge checks do not prove that secured Elasticsearch functionality survived initialization or bundle restore.
successful_path: Verify unauthenticated auth challenge only as a readiness sign, then require authenticated root JSON, green cluster health, smoke index creation and document indexing/search, plus successful read-only search using a non-admin user after portable redeploy.
fix: Create one read-only verification user and include it in the final bundle docs.
Use the bundled CA cert for every curl verification path.
precheck: Ensure the verify script bypasses local proxies with curl --noproxy '*'.
anti_pattern: Do not accept HTTP reachability alone as Elasticsearch success.
quick_checks: GET / with elastic credentials returns cluster metadata.
Search on apdv1-smoke returns the seeded verification document for both elastic and the read-only user.

summary: For Nagios Core 4.5.12, a reliable acceptance gate combines the authenticated `/nagios/` shell, one critical stylesheet fetch, `/nagios/main.php`, and the localhost `HTTP` service showing `HTTP OK` on `status.cgi?host=localhost`.
symptom: A Nagios deployment can appear up while the daemon, UI asset path, or bundled localhost monitoring baseline is still not proven usable.
root_cause: Weak checks that stop at container health or one authenticated page miss whether the operator UI and a real service check are both functioning.
successful_path: Authenticate to `/nagios/`, fetch `/nagios/stylesheets/common.css`, fetch `/nagios/main.php`, then require the localhost `HTTP` service to show `HTTP OK` on the status CGI page before accepting either the primary deployment or the portable bundle.
fix: Use `curl --noproxy '*' -u 'nagiosadmin:<password>'` for all localhost checks.
Require the localhost `HTTP` service row on `status.cgi?host=localhost` to contain `HTTP OK: HTTP/1.1 200 OK`.
precheck: Allow the sample localhost profile enough time to leave the initial `PENDING` state before classifying the deployment.
Verify the authenticated CSS asset before assuming the web UI is complete.
anti_pattern: Accepting a healthy container or authenticated shell alone without proving a monitored localhost service has reached `OK`.

summary: A strong verification gate for Metaflow UI 1.3.14 checks the HTML shell, hashed JS/CSS assets, UI-backend CORS, and a real HelloFlow run exposed through the UI backend after metadata-service initialization.
symptom: Simple root-page or health checks can miss a broken UI/backend boundary or an empty UI with no real Metaflow data.
root_cause: Metaflow UI depends on a separate UI backend and on real metadata rows; the root HTML alone does not prove the browser can query flows and runs successfully.
successful_path: Require HTTP 200 for the UI root and hashed JS/CSS assets, verify Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the frontend origin on /flows when the frontend is served separately, execute a real HelloFlow run through the metadata service, and confirm /flows, /flows/HelloFlow/runs/1, tasks, and metadata all return the expected data.
fix: Pair shell-and-asset checks with UI-backend data checks after a real sample flow run.
Record one direct metadata-service health endpoint and one migration-status endpoint alongside the UI evidence.
precheck: If the frontend and UI backend are on different ports, verify CORS explicitly before assuming the browser path works.
Populate at least one real flow/run before declaring the UI usable.
anti_pattern: Do not treat an empty /flows response as sufficient proof of a usable Metaflow UI deployment.
Do not stop at root HTML 200 without fetching a referenced asset and checking flow/run data.
